Header:
Date: 2028-10-02
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Reed (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Kumar (Celestial - Head of Platform), Sofia Delgado (Celestial - Lead ML Eng), Tom Weller (Celestial - Infra Ops)
Shared: Redwood one-pager (link: https://redwood.ai/docs/one-pager), SOC2 packet (sent after call)

Summary (auto): quick integration discovery focused on SDKs and orchestration. Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for user-facing chat features. Primary concerns: observability hooks, gateway/proxy compatibility, rate limits, and LangChain/LlamaIndex support. Next: share pricing, security docs, and repo samples; schedule technical deep-dive.

Topics: SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex, gateway/proxy, rate limits/quotas, observability/tracing hooks, Dedicated capacity sizing, SaaS vs VPC tradeoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Ethan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Maya's our solutions engineer, she'll jump into the technical bits.
[00:12] Ravi: Yeah thanks for doing this. We wanted to do a quick discovery to understand how Redwood would fit into our stack, we're evaluating a couple of options.
[00:20] Maya: Great, maybe quickly — can you give us a 2 minute run through of the use case and current infra?
[00:27] Sofia: Sure. We're building a user-facing chat assistant for our customer portal, mostly retrieval-augmented generation on top of internal docs and product data. Right now we prototype with OpenAI hosted and we've stitched Lang Chain flows for RAG, and LlamaIndex as an indexing layer for some teams. But we're seeing latency and cost pressure at scale.
[00:44] Tom: Also we have strict network topology, all egress goes through an internal gateway/proxy, and we have per-tenant rate limits at the gateway level. So we need compatibility or a path for Private or VPC deployments.
[00:58] Ethan: Perfect, that's right in the scope of what we see. A few qualification Qs: what's your expected QPS for the first 6 months and SLA needs?
[01:08] Ravi: Ballpark is 40-80 requests per second at peak, average prompt sizes are 350-700 tokens, with a couple of heavier workflows hitting up to 2k tokens. We need 99.9% availability and P95 latency under 600ms for short prompts.
[01:25] Maya: And what about caching/prefix reuse — do you have repeated prompts per user or heavily unique queries?
[01:31] Sofia: Mix. Most are repeat-ish flows for troubleshooting and config, but we will have long-tail unique queries once we expand. We plan to use caching heavily.
[01:40] Maya: Ok good. On the integration side, Redwood offers SDKs in JS and Python, and we have example connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. Our SDKs support both direct REST and streaming websocket responses. We also provide a small gateway shim for customers that need proxy integration.
[01:57] Tom: When you say shim, is that something that runs in our VPC? We're not ok with open egress.
[02:04] Maya: Yes — we have two patterns: Hosted API with customer-side gateway/proxy rules (TLS to Redwood, mTLS optional for Enterprise), or Redwood Private where the control plane is managed but the runtime sits in your VPC/on-prem. The shim is a lightweight sidecar you can run to translate your gateway headers to Redwood routing headers — it doesn't send logs unless you opt-in.
[02:25] Ravi: That sounds promising. How do you handle rate-limiting? We have per-tenant quotas and want to avoid cascading 429s.
[02:33] Ethan: We support token-based quotas, request quotas, and route-level throttles. On Dedicated we can enforce per-API-key rate limits at the edge and also configure backpressure/queueing on the runtime. For Private you control the edge layer entirely; we surface metrics so you can map your tenant IDs to Redwood usage.
[02:50] Sofia: Do you expose a webhook or push metric for per-tenant usage? We need to feed our billing and telemetry.
[02:57] Maya: Yes. We have observability hooks: Prometheus endpoints inside Dedicated/Private, event webhooks for usage events, and a usage API for aggregated and per-request logs. For Hosted we provide streamed usage logs and a data export. The tracing hooks support open-telemetry so you can correlate with your existing traces.
[03:15] Tom: Any gotchas with our proxy? We use a custom gateway that mutates X-Forwarded-* headers and enforces an internal session header.
[03:23] Maya: That's fine but sometimes auto-transcription will show header names differently — we've seen X-Request-ID turn into RequestID on some shims — you can map them in the shim config. Also note KV cache behavior can be sensitive to header changes if you key caching on user header. (slight laugh) It's the K-V cash, sometimes spelled K V cash in logs haha — but seriously we give you mapping rules.
[03:46] Ravi: Right. On the model side, do you host open models? We want the option to use an LLM that's quantized on GPUs in Dedicated.
[03:53] Maya: Yup. We maintain a model catalog with curated open models and model variants optimized for different hardware. On Dedicated we can pin a quantized variant and we handle kernel selection and sequence-length optimizations. For customers who need the ultimate latency, we recommend model variants with 4-bit quantization and a KV-cache optimized runtime.
[04:12] Sofia: How mature are the LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations? We rely heavily on LlamaIndex for doc ingest pipelines.
[04:19] Maya: We have maintained connector examples for both. For LangChain we support the standard chains and callbacks; for LlamaIndex we have an adapter that handles chunking and metadata preservation. We also maintain a sample repo that wraps retries, batching, and backoff best practices for high throughput. I'll send that repo after the call.
[04:36] Sophia: Please do — we've had to patch rate-limit handling in LangChain ourselves.
[04:40] Ethan: On the SDK side, two notes: our JS SDK supports streaming tokens with incremental deltas and function-calling semantics; the Python SDK has first-class asyncio support and higher-level wrappers for RAG. Both have sample notebooks for LangChain/LlamaIndex.
[04:57] Ravi: Great. For Dedicated sizing — do you have a quick rule-of-thumb? 40-80 qps with 350-700 token prompts, and 2k for heavy flows.
[05:07] Maya: Roughly, for a 40-80 qps steady load with mixed prompt lengths, you'd likely start with a small Dedicated pool (N x A100 equivalent) depending on model choice. The right approach is to run a short benchmark — we can do a 24-hour POC on a trial Dedicated pool, run your sample traces, and produce a latency/cost profile. That helps pick quantization and batch sizes.
[05:26] Tom: For the POC, would we need to open firewall rules to Redwood? We prefer the runtime inside our VPC if possible.
[05:33] Maya: For Private deployment yes the runtime sits inside your VPC and we do a one-time setup with your infra team. For Dedicated hosted we need to allow egress to Redwood control-plane endpoints; the runtime can be dedicated hardware managed by us but in the cloud region.
[05:46] Ethan: On security: we support SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS integrations for customer key management, and detailed audit logs. We'll include SOC2 and ISO docs in the follow-up.
[05:56] Sofia: How granular are the audit logs? We need per-request metadata and user-id mapping so we can comply with our audit policies.
[06:03] Maya: We emit per-request logs in JSON with request-id, api-key, tenant id, timestamps, latencies, and model variant. You can also stream these to your SIEM.
[06:12] Ravi: One more thing — observability hooks: can we instrument token-level cost breakdowns to attribute spend per tenant?
[06:19] Maya: Yes. We provide token counts and per-token cost estimates in the usage API plus attribution tags so you can cost-center by tenant or route.
[06:28] Tom: Any limits on the gateway shim throughput? If we put it in front of our proxy, it needs to handle big bursts.
[06:35] Maya: The shim is lightweight and stateless; it scales horizontally. For heavy bursts we recommend fronting it with your existing load balancer and making it autoscale. For Dedicated we can expose an ingress balancer that handles burst absorb.
[06:48] Sofia: We also have an internal requirement for canary rollouts and model version pinning for A/B testing. How does Redwood handle rollouts?
[06:56] Ethan: We support route-level rollouts, canary percentages, and automatic fallback policies. You can pin a route to a model version and gradually shift traffic while monitoring objective metrics. The Console has per-route dashboards and rollout controls.
[07:08] Ravi: Perfect. Ok next steps then?
[07:12] Ethan: We'll send: pricing matrix (hosted vs dedicated vs private), SOC2/ISO docs, LangChain/LlamaIndex sample repo, and propose a 2-hour technical deep-dive to run through your gateway config and a short benchmark run. Maya will prepare the repo and a benchmark plan.
[07:26] Sofia: Sounds good. Can you include an example prompt set and sample throughput script so we can see how to reproduce?
[07:32] Maya: Yes, I'll include prompts and a load script.
[07:35] Tom: We'll pull the gateway/proxy config and share it.
[07:38] Ethan: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up in an email.
[07:42] Ravi: Appreciate it.
[07:45] (call ends)
